speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand your symptoms better to help you; could you tell me exactly when your right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls started? Also, have you noticed any specific changes in your memory or behavior, such as forgetfulness or paranoia, around the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Subacute Cerebellar Degeneration (likely associated with Small Cell Lung Cancer)

The sudden onset of right leg weakness and unsteady gait coinciding with significant memory loss and paranoia over the past six months is highly concerning for a paraneoplastic syndrome affecting the cerebellum and cognitive function. Given your age and the rapid progression of these neurological and psychiatric symptoms, we need to rule out an underlying malignancy immediately. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Tumor Markers (CEA, NSE, ProGRP), and a Chest CT scan. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI.
